To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distribution of ready-to-use therapeutic food in a population-based setting was effective in reducing wasting and severe wasting among children aged 6-60 months.

the distribution of RUTF in the months before harvest reduced the incidence of wasting by 36.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 17.5% to 51.9%; P =.002) and of severe wasting by 57.8% (95% CI, 32.1% to 74.7%; P <.001) among children aged 6 through 60 months in Niger compared with a control intervention.

a community-based distribution of a lipidbased nutrient supplement to children aged 6 through 60 months during the lean season in a population with a high burden of child wasting reduced wasting and severe wasting by about 40% and 60%, respectively, compared with a control population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prevention and treatment of child wasting and undernutrition.
the prevention of wasting and the promotion of child growth.
the prevention of child malnutrition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

targeted distribution of RUF T to children with wasting is efficacious for the treatment of severe acute wasting, and targeted distribution of RUT F to children without wasting in areas with seasonal or acute food shortages is effective for the prevention of acute wasting in children.

the targeted distribution of ready-to-use therapeutic food to children in a population-based setting in Niger was associated with improved weight maintenance and reduced prevalence of wasting and severe wasting among the children in the intervention villages.
the use of RUTF for prevention of wasting in young children is efficacious but the cost-effectiveness and sustainability of the intervention compared with other interventions is not known.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distribution of RUTF in this setting was associated with improved weight gain and reduced wasting.

we need to consider a variety of approaches for preventing malnutrition, including targeted and untargeted interventions, and that we need to continue to improve and evaluate interventions that have the potential to improve the nutritional status of children in the long term.
the use of RUTF to prevent wasting in children aged less than 5 years is an important addition to the arsenal of interventions to reduce malnutrition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of RUTF in the villages where we implemented this study was efficacious in reducing wasting and severe wasting.
the use of RUTF in a community setting is an effective strategy to improve the nutritional status of young children in a setting of food insecurity.
RUTF can be used as a preventive intervention in the context of food shortages.
